quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.explanation: Locked brakes can cause you to lose control. If your front brake locks, release it and apply it again. If your rear brake locks on a good surface while stopping, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: It is illegal to ride a motorcycle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: In California, riders age 21 and older cannot ride with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Riders under 21 cannot ride with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. Even below the legal limit, alcohol can make riding unsafe.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: Drinking fast causes alcohol to build up in your body quickly. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol stays in your system.

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before turning. Taking a turn too fast can cause you to drift out of your lane or off the road.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your hands ready over the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready over the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Ride carefully when approaching an intersection. Keep your hands ready over the clutch and both brakes so you can react quickly if needed.

questions.question: For a motorcycle operator, a helmet is:

options.text: Not required if you have ridden for more than two years.

questions.explanation: In Virginia, motorcycle operators and passengers must wear helmets. A proper helmet is the best protection against head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: For motorcycle operators, helmets are:
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet whenever you operate a motorcycle.

questions.question: If you ride behind another vehicle at night, you can see bumps in the road ahead by:

options.text: Listening to the other vehicle scraping the pavement.
Watching the other vehicle's taillights bounce.
Watching the rear bumper to see if it bounces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watching the other vehicle's taillights bounce.
questions.explanation: Watch the vehicle ahead to see the road conditions at night. If its taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps ahead on the road.

questions.question: Motorcycle mirrors:

options.text: Have blind spots, just like car mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like car mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you best.
Move to the part of the lane closest to the traffic sign.
Move to the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you best.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position yourself so other drivers can see you as early as possible.

questions.question: How do you shift up to a higher gear?

options.text: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift it.
Place your foot over the shift lever and push it.
Use your thumb to move the lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift it.
questions.explanation: To shift to a higher gear, put your foot under the shift lever and lift it.

questions.question: When should you use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch?

options.text: When the throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
When you start to lose control in a curve.
When the motorcycle starts to wobble.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it, turn off the engine and pull in the clutch right away. This removes power from the rear wheel so you can safely stop.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Your mirrors can show you everything around you.
Turn your head to check your blind spot and use your mirrors.
Signal and immediately move to the right or left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot and use your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot in addition to using your mirrors before changing lanes.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: As your motorcycle goes faster, what must you do?
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle speeds up, you must shift into higher gears.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
Only stop to let other traffic pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, let all traffic and pedestrians cross, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: They are safer than when used alone.
Their effects can be stronger than when used alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their effects can be stronger than when used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make it unsafe to ride. Some drugs become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: What does the SEE strategy stand for?
questions.explanation: The SEE strategy helps riders make safe choices. It stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe while riding?

options.text: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Scan the road far ahead to spot dangers before you reach them. This helps you avoid problems while riding.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When should you do a safety check on your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Always check your motorcycle before you ride. Small problems are more dangerous on a motorcycle than on a car.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Allow you to blend in with traffic.
Encourage others to use your lane.

questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should stop other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: Is hearing protection important for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can harm your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection every time you ride to protect your hearing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that go under 25 mph. Examples include construction equipment, farm machines, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do at a blind intersection?

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Ignore the stop line and move forward to see better.
Stop at the stop line and then go through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection with a stop line or sign, stop where marked. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.
